children: Banks open Sunday, September 27, as PSBs and RRBs provide an additional banking day ahead of the proposed three-day bank strike

Public sector banks (PSBs) and regional rural banks (RRBs) will remain open on Sunday, September 27, as the government moves to limit disruption from a proposed three-day nationwide bank strike beginning September 28. The Reserve Bank of India has approved the opening of bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests on the Sunday, providing customers an additional banking day before the strike.

The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU), which claims to represent around 90 per cent of the banking workforce, has called the strike from September 28 to 30, primarily demanding implementation of a five-day banking week. The proposed action also coincides with the September 30 half-yearly closing, when banks undertake reconciliation, provisioning and treasury and market operations.
Sunday Opening To Offset Extended Disruption

The government’s decision comes after September 26 and 27 would otherwise have been weekend holidays, potentially creating an effective five-day interruption when combined with the three-day strike. The Finance Ministry said the Sunday opening was intended to ensure that customers’ genuine banking requirements were not adversely affected for an extended period.

Banks have also been asked to prepare for the strike and maintain continuity of essential services. Several state-run lenders, including State Bank of India, Union Bank of India, Indian Bank and Punjab National Bank, have issued advisories asking customers to complete important transactions ahead of the strike. Banks are also directing customers towards ATMs, business correspondent points, internet banking, mobile banking and UPI for routine requirements.

The strike follows a one-day nationwide action on September 11. The unions have maintained that they will proceed with the September 28-30 strike after discussions with the government and bank managements failed to resolve the five-day banking demand.

The unions had also raised issues relating to pensions, dearness allowance and the option for employees covered under the National Pension System to shift to the old pension scheme. The government has kept the Performance Linked Incentive scheme for PSB executives in abeyance, but the five-day banking issue remains under consideration.

The timing of the proposed strike is significant for banks and businesses because September 30 marks the half-yearly closing. Any disruption could affect branch-based transactions and activities linked to reconciliation, provisioning and treasury operations. An indefinite strike has also been announced from October 26 if the unions’ demands remain unresolved.
